findings.issue: The idem key is USER_DELETED:<userId> and the insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the outbox never sends a second USER_DELETED for the same user id. If an account is ever restored and deleted again, or an operator resets a request to SCHEDULED after new data was written, user-service erases its own rows and marks the request COMPLETED, but no new event is written. Downstream services would keep any PII created after the first event. The design accepts this because auth-service disables deleted accounts, but nothing in code makes it visible.
findings.fix: Log at WARN when enqueue inserts 0 rows (update() returns 0), so the suppressed event shows up. Alternatively key the event on the deletion request (for example USER_DELETED:<userId>:<deletion_request id or completed_at>) so each completed request emits one event. Also record the assumption in ADR 0011.

findings.issue: describe() stores the Kafka root-cause message truncated to 500 characters but not redacted. I checked what Kafka and Spring Kafka put in these messages: TimeoutException (metadata or delivery), RecordTooLargeException (sizes) and KafkaProducerException ('Failed to send') carry the topic, sizes and sometimes broker host:port, never the record value. The payload is only UUIDs and a timestamp anyway, so no email or PII can reach last_error. Broker hostnames can, and they are shown to ADMIN callers and written to WARN/ERROR logs. That is a low infrastructure-disclosure risk.
findings.fix: Optional: keep only the root-cause class name in the admin response, or strip host:port patterns. No change is needed for PII.

summary: I found no blockers or major issues, so I approve this SHA. Erasure is atomic: assertNoBlockers runs outside the transaction, and one TransactionTemplate wraps the guarded SCHEDULED->COMPLETED claim, the profile anonymisation, the 10 erasure statements and the outbox enqueue. Nothing inside the callback catches the rollback. Neither JobLock (a session advisory lock on its own connection, no transaction) nor runDue opens an outer transaction, so each user commits or rolls back alone. forcedFailureRollsBack proves the request stays SCHEDULED with the PII intact. The new endpoints GET /api/users/admin/outbox and POST /{id}/retry have no public permit and fall under the service's own anyRequest().authenticated() chain, with class-level @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) and @EnableMethodSecurity active. The tests send a 'roles' claim through the real PlatformJwtAuthenticationConverter and get ROLE_ADMIN, and they assert 401 and 403 on both GET and POST. IDOR does not apply because this is a global admin-only resource. Status is whitelisted to PENDING or DEAD and the id is bound as a typed UUID, and all SQL uses bound parameters, so there is no injection path. The 200-row cap is in place, the response has no payload field, and retry only moves DEAD rows (404 otherwise). On PII: the payload holds eventId, type, userId and occurredAt only. A corrupt payload is reported as the constant text 'Corrupt outbox payload' and Jackson's message is dropped. Logs carry only the userId UUID. Kafka exception messages do not include record values, and the value has no PII anyway. On duplicates: the stored payload is re-sent with the same eventId on redelivery or retry. The consumers in payment, promotion and seller are tested as idempotent, and the claim UPDATE with the idem key blocks double enqueue. V6 only adds a table and indexes, with no ALTER or DROP. The diff adds no secrets and no dependencies; the Jackson 2 ObjectMapper is already on the classpath. The diff also leaves SecurityConfig, the gateway and PrivacyKafkaConfig unchanged.
